He can certainly challenge the admissibility of the documents. He should do that in a timely manner when the document is tendered, and not after the witness has left the courtroom, and then to speculate or throw out arguments that really should have been put to the witness. He made the decision not to cross-examine the witnesses. He must live by the consequences of his decision. The Trial Chamber repeatedly has discussed this issue with him, it's clear that he has made a knowing decision to waive his right to cross-examine, and now he's stuck with that decision and the implications of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you can have the floor, Mr. Seselj, but there are two things: There is the substance and the form. You are right as to the form. You are right in saying that you object to the admission of a document for various reasons. Mr. Mundis is right in that. But as to the substance, Mr. Mundis says that you cannot wait until the witness is out of the courtroom to go to the heart of matters. There's no problem. I'm sure you're bound to agree with that. So, Mr. Seselj, you had another thing to mention.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. No, I first have to respond to Mr. Mundis. I thank Mr. Mundis for the compliment of noting the intelligence behind my action, and I'm sorry I cannot return the compliment, because his position cannot be called particularly intelligent. What I have stated has nothing to do whatsoever with cross-examination. My objection is based on the form of the document that has been tendered, and my speculation on the substance of the statement are based on the inappropriateness of the form. I can go on speculating forever, as it is my right to speculate forever, because I have this statement in inappropriate form, which is the fault of the Prosecution. You should have thought about it when you were doing it. When you look at this certification made by an officer of the Tribunal, you will see that there is a rubric called "Additional Notes." Why wasn't this used to indicate that the witness had made additions to her statement? Why has this addition been made so irregularly, just put in the binder any which way? Why doesn't it state, on one separate page, that the witness has supplemented her statement? Why wouldn't I speculate? I will go on speculating forever, because the Prosecution is simply laying themselves open to this by their gullibility, by their lack of thought, and I will go on speculating forever. This has nothing to do with this witness. This is a critique of your work and your action. It is so unlawful that the Trial Chamber should have sanctioned it long ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On that particular point, that was raised a while ago. Admittedly, Mr. Mundis, when the 92 bis procedure was considered by the Prosecution, and we have some evidence of this, the presiding officer, as per the Rules, came to see the witness and asked the witness to fill in a form. The procedure is very clear. Then once this is done, you can ask for the statement to be admitted under 92 bis. You could have done it in this particular case, but what happened is that sometime later, for some reason, the witness gave additional supplementary information to a previous statement. Legally speaking, the same presiding officer should have conducted this additional procedure, but here we have a document which raises some questions. We don't know whether you introduced that document later. If it was then accepted by the presiding officer later, that's not acceptable. Or is it the case that the presiding officer or the Registry produced this document after being called by the witness [as interpreted]? We don't know. There is something that's beyond any doubt. The Registry is in charge of 92 bis procedure, and that's why the document we have here attached to this statement raises a lot of questions. I'm not blaming anyone. I'm just stating the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think you got this one squarely on the head. It's an issue for the Registrar. They're the ones who appoint the presiding officers, at the request of one of the parties; and the procedure that is undertaken in terms of certifying a statement pursuant to Rule 92 bis is one which falls within the scope of the Registry. I am unable, at this point in time - I can certainly make some further inquiries, if it would be helpful - but at this point in time, I'm certainly not in a position to provide the Trial Chamber with any specific facts relating to this particular statement which was certified under Rule 92 bis. If the Trial Chamber would like some further information or clarification, I will undertake to provide that information as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you could, of course, it would be very useful for the Trial Chamber, and Mr. Seselj should be notified as well. Yes, indeed, it's possible that the Registrar did this. It's possible. We are now going to give the floor to Mr. Seselj for the rest of his comments.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have more to say about this, Mr. President. We see, from this certification, that the witness had confirmed that the contents of her written statement is true, to the best of her knowledge. We know that this witness statement also contains an affirmation that she's Serbian; whereas, she's not. Now, in the additional remarks in this declaration, there is nothing, it's empty. But on the same day, it's on the same day that the additional statement was made, without any official marks. What does this mean, then? It's complete frivolity in the actions of the Prosecution. If the witness had corrected her statement in the presence of an officer of the Registry, then he should have stated so in the declaration, "The witness corrected this, this, and that." Otherwise, when the officer of the Registry took the signature on this declaration and went to lunch in the nearby tavern, maybe then the OTP representative took this additional statement in his absence. You're going to say I'm speculating again, but it's only natural that the officer of the Registry wrote this declaration and went out to lunch. Then the representative of the OTP decided there's something else to be squeezed out of this witness and stayed with her to work. Yes, I'm speculating, but why are you acting in this way and giving me food for speculation? This is not pointless, senseless speculation. All this is speculation based on legal principle, because you acted unlawfully. You are giving me a field day. Of course, I'm going to use it. You can't blame me for using it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor will make some inquiries, Mr. Seselj, and will tell us exactly what happened. But you wanted to raise a second point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you remember, Mr. President, and I know your colleagues are aware of it as well, the indictment against me was brought in January 2003, the motion to extend it was submitted in May 2004, and the whole thing was finalised in May 2005. Then in 2006, the Trial Chamber ordered the indictment to be abbreviated, throwing out certain locations, leaving the possibility open to the Prosecution that they may lead evidence on those locations that were thrown out, if they can see a pattern of behaviour within the framework of the joint criminal enterprise, but the judgement cannot be based on that. I'll give you only two examples: Today's witness and Jelena Radosevic who was here two or three weeks ago. They did not testify to any pattern of conduct. They did not testify to any joint criminal enterprise. Their testimony could be called auxiliary crime-based testimony, because they don't really have any idea about crime-base evidence. They don't know who was killed, they can't identify anyone, et cetera. This is abuse of procedure. The Prosecution should follow your instructions, and concerning these locations, they should only lead evidence on the pattern of conduct, not lead pointless evidence. What can you do with this evidence? Of course, it's only grist to my mill that you, Mr. President, established, in talking to the witness, that the theory of the Prosecution, that members of the Serbian Radical Party had killed those four witnesses, is totally unfounded, because the witness herself says that she doesn't know who killed these Croats. So it's useful to me, but I'm putting to you the problem in principle. If the indictment was shortened to save time, then where is this economy? The list of witnesses has not been reduced by a single name. There is no economy in time. Why, then, was the decision made? I asked you to review that decision, as the Presiding Judge, part of the then-Trial Chamber before the trial began, and you refused it. That decision remained. What is all this for, to fill time because the Prosecution has no relevant witnesses? I had to make this objection, although what we had today was extremely useful to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the pattern of conduct is provided for at Rule 93: "Evidence of a consistent pattern of conduct relevant to serious violations of international humanitarian law under the Statute may be admissible in the interest of justice," paragraph A. Paragraph B of Rule 93: "Acts tending to show such a pattern of conduct shall be disclosed by the Prosecutor to the Defence pursuant to Rule 66." Of course, interpretation of this Rule is required. From what I understand from the decision of Trial Chamber I, the Prosecutor for some locations is allowed to produce witnesses whose evidence will enable the Trial Chamber Judges to establish the existence of a consistent pattern of conduct from such-and-such date to such-and-such date, and this may also include joint criminal enterprise and other things. It's quite complicated to interpret Rule 93. It can be stated that some evidence can be used to demonstrate that crimes were committed in some municipalities. In any case, this lady came to talk about the events in Vocin in 1991. That's what we can clearly see from her testimony. Next week, we have three witnesses scheduled. I'm not going to give their names because you can never be too cautious. Some of these witnesses may be protected witnesses. You're on your feet, Mr. Mundis. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I only want to assist the Trial Chamber with what Mr. Seselj said. He said that, which is true, Vocin was a removed municipality and we're allowed to lead pattern evidence. Just for the evidence of the Trial Chamber, when this decision came out, we reduced our witness list tremendously. Formerly, we had 130 witness, and now we have only about 100. And only for Vocin, we removed 11 witnesses which were seen once, and now the remaining ones are coming here to give pattern evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just wanted to confirm the letter as it went out, I believe, yesterday with the list of the three witnesses who are scheduled to appear next week. I simply at this stage confirm the information that's listed in that letter, and those three witnesses are scheduled for next week and we have no indications of any problems at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three witnesses, maybe one a day. How much time will you need for these witnesses? Do you have any idea about how much time you will need for each one of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe, with respect to VS-26, the Prosecution needs 1.5 hours, one and a half hours. For witness Strinovic, we will endeavour, as we have been doing recently with respect to experts, to keep that evidence as short as possible, perhaps 35 minutes, 40 minutes. With respect to Witness VS-1093, he is listed for two hours, and we will certainly endeavor to move that as expeditiously as possible. So I don't believe we'll have any problems with respect to next week. We're still waiting for the Trial Chamber's decision with respect to the expert, but I don't believe we'll have any problems in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decision will be issued. Based on my personal view of the matter, but the Trial Chamber is examining it, we have four expert witnesses left in the 65 ter list. We have identified four expert witnesses, so after the following one, we'll have three left. I believe that 30 to 45 minutes will be amply sufficient, especially since we are talking about expert in technical matters, in technical fields. Of course, we'll give Mr. Seselj all the time he needs for the cross-examination of these witnesses. Mr. Seselj, is there anything else you would like to raise? No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we'll need a redaction here. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
